steps.name: Build factorial DESeq2 object and QC
caveats: Alphabetical factor ordering would silently make KO the reference genotype and drug the reference treatment, inverting the sign of every reported log2 fold change
Gene symbols as row identifiers can contain duplicates; silently keeping the first occurrence loses counts
With n=4 per cell, apparent PCA outliers are common noise and dropping them is more harmful than keeping them
steps.context: 2x2 factorial human brain bulk RNA-seq, genotype (WT, KO) x treatment (vehicle, drug), n=4 per cell, 16 samples total, raw salmon gene-level counts on gene symbols. The research question is the interaction, so the model must be fitted with the interaction term from the start; the QC exists to establish that the factorial structure is intact before that test is trusted.
steps.question: Do the 16 samples in counts.csv match the 16 rows of metadata.csv, and does the WT/KO x vehicle/drug structure hold up under library-size, PCA and sample-distance QC before any interaction test is run?
constraints: Use DESeq2 in R; do not use pydeseq2 for this step
Set factor reference levels explicitly with relevel — do not rely on alphabetical ordering (which would make KO and drug the references)
Fit the design with the interaction term ~genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment; do not fit an additive model as the primary object
Do not remove any sample from the analysis in this step
steps.description: Load /eval-four-models-without-interaction-2x2-n4-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 16 sample columns, first column gene symbol, raw integer salmon counts) and /eval-four-models-without-interaction-2x2-n4-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (16 rows x 4 columns: sample id, genotype, treatment, condition). Verify sample identifiers match one-to-one and reorder metadata to counts column order — never assume the order is already aligned. Collapse duplicate gene symbols (sum counts) if any exist and report how many. Build a DESeq2 DESeqDataSet with design ~genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, setting factor reference levels explicitly to genotype=WT and treatment=vehicle. Confirm the 4x4 design table (4 replicates per genotype x treatment cell) and print it. Pre-filter to genes with at least 10 counts in at least 4 samples. Run estimateSizeFactors and the full DESeq fit; save the fitted object (RDS) plus normalized counts and a VST matrix for downstream steps. QC outputs: per-sample library size barplot, size factors, VST PCA (PC1-PC2, points shaped by genotype and coloured by treatment, plus a version labelled by sample id), sample-sample Euclidean distance heatmap, and dispersion plot. Flag any sample that separates from its own cell on PCA or has a library size deviating more than ~3-fold from the median, but do NOT drop samples — report them, since with n=4 per cell removing one sample materially damages the interaction test.
acceptance_criteria: Sample identifiers in counts.csv columns and metadata.csv rows are confirmed matched one-to-one and metadata is reordered to counts order; any mismatch is reported explicitly
Design table printed showing 4 samples in each of the four genotype x treatment cells (WT/vehicle, WT/drug, KO/vehicle, KO/drug)
Reference levels reported as genotype=WT and treatment=vehicle, and resultsNames() of the fitted object is printed including the genotypeKO.treatmentdrug interaction coefficient
Number of genes retained after low-count filtering reported out of 12000
Saved artifacts: fitted DESeqDataSet (RDS), normalized count matrix, VST matrix
QC figures produced: library size barplot, VST PCA coloured by treatment and shaped by genotype, sample-distance heatmap, dispersion plot
Any candidate outlier sample is named with its evidence, and it is stated that no samples were removed

steps.name: Interaction test and within-genotype drug contrasts
caveats: The interaction test has roughly half the effective power of a main effect at the same n; with n=4 per cell a null interaction result is entirely plausible and must not be spun as a positive
Sign conventions: with WT and vehicle as references, a positive interaction LFC means the drug effect is more positive in KO than in WT
A skewed or spiked interaction p-value histogram indicates model misspecification or unmodelled batch structure and must be reported
steps.context: Primary hypothesis of the study. The interaction term is the formal test of 'does the drug act differently in KO than WT'. The within-genotype contrasts are needed for interpretation but are not themselves evidence of an interaction — a gene significant in KO and not in WT is not the same as a significant difference between the two effects, and this must be stated in the output.
steps.question: Which genes show a genotype-dependent drug response — i.e. a significant genotypeKO:treatmentdrug interaction — and what is the drug effect separately within WT and within KO?
constraints: Report unadjusted and BH-adjusted p-values from the unshrunken Wald/LRT statistics; use shrunken LFCs only for ranking and plotting
Use apeglm shrinkage only for coefficients present in resultsNames; use ashr for the difference-of-differences contrast
Do not declare a genotype-specific drug effect on the basis of within-genotype contrasts alone

If zero genes pass FDR<0.05 on the interaction, report that as the finding — do not lower the threshold silently, but do report the FDR<0.1 count and the top-ranked genes by interaction p-value as exploratory
steps.description: Using the fitted DESeqDataSet from T1S1, extract the primary result: the interaction coefficient genotypeKO.treatmentdrug (Wald test, alpha=0.05, BH-adjusted), which directly answers whether the drug acts differently in KO than in WT. Cross-check it with a likelihood-ratio test comparing full ~genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment against reduced ~genotype + treatment, and report the concordance between the two gene rankings (number of genes FDR<0.05 under each, overlap). Then refit or re-parameterise using a single combined cell-means factor group = genotype_treatment (four levels: WT_vehicle, WT_drug, KO_vehicle, KO_drug) with design ~group, and extract from that one fit: (a) drug vs vehicle within WT, (b) drug vs vehicle within KO, (c) KO_vehicle vs WT_vehicle (baseline genotype effect), and (d) the difference-of-differences contrast, confirming that (d) matches the interaction coefficient from the factorial fit. Apply lfcShrink (apeglm for coefficients, ashr for arbitrary contrasts) for effect-size ranking, but report unshrunken p-values and adjusted p-values for inference. Write one tidy results table per contrast (gene symbol, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, shrunken LFC, stat, pvalue, padj) and a merged wide table keyed on gene symbol carrying all four contrasts. Report the number of genes at FDR<0.05 and at FDR<0.1 for each contrast. Produce MA plots and volcano plots per contrast and a p-value histogram for the interaction test to check calibration.
acceptance_criteria: Interaction results table for genotypeKO.treatmentdrug written with per-gene padj; the number of genes at FDR<0.05 and FDR<0.1 reported explicitly, including the case of zero
LRT (full vs additive-reduced) run and its significant-gene count and overlap with the Wald interaction result reported
Cell-means ~group fit produces the four contrasts (drug-vs-vehicle in WT, drug-vs-vehicle in KO, KO-vs-WT at vehicle, difference-of-differences)
Difference-of-differences contrast is verified numerically consistent with the factorial interaction coefficient (log2FC agreement reported)
Merged wide results table across contrasts written, keyed on gene symbol
MA and volcano plots per contrast plus a p-value histogram for the interaction test
Output states in plain language that significance within one genotype and non-significance within the other does not by itself establish an interaction

steps.name: Classify interaction patterns and quantify power
caveats: The 'KO-specific response' class is the most seductive and least reliable — it is defined partly by a non-significant result in WT, which is not evidence of absence
With n=4 the dispersion estimates themselves are noisy, so the power estimate is an approximation and should be reported with that caveat
steps.context: Turns the interaction statistics into interpretable biology and bounds the negative result. With 12,000 genes and 16 samples, the multiple-testing burden on a low-power interaction term is the dominant constraint on what can be claimed.
steps.question: Among genes with evidence of a genotype-dependent drug response, which show a KO-specific response, a WT-specific response, a magnitude-only difference, or an opposite-direction (antagonistic) response — and what effect size could this 4-per-cell design have detected?
constraints: Classification must use the interaction padj as the gate for classes 1-4; do not classify on within-genotype significance alone
Use the VST matrix from T1S1 for heatmaps, not raw or log-raw counts
Label every gene list derived without interaction-term significance as exploratory in the output
steps.description: Take the merged contrast table from T1S2 and classify genes into interaction patterns using the within-WT and within-KO drug log2 fold changes together with the interaction padj: (1) KO-specific — significant drug response in KO, not in WT, interaction FDR<0.05; (2) WT-specific — the mirror; (3) opposite direction — drug LFC signs differ between genotypes with interaction FDR<0.05; (4) magnitude-only — same sign, different magnitude, interaction FDR<0.05; (5) shared response — significant drug effect in both, interaction not significant. Report counts in every class, and write the class-annotated table. Visualise with a scatter of WT drug LFC vs KO drug LFC (points coloured by interaction significance, with the y=x identity line), and a heatmap of VST values for the top interaction genes with samples ordered WT_vehicle, WT_drug, KO_vehicle, KO_drug and rows scaled, plus per-gene normalized-count dot plots for the top ~12 interaction genes to show the four cell means directly. Add a power/sensitivity statement: using the observed per-gene dispersions from T1S1 and n=4 per cell, estimate by simulation or by the standard negative-binomial approximation the interaction log2 fold change detectable at 80% power and FDR<0.05 for a typically expressed gene, and report it. This calibrates any negative result.
acceptance_criteria: Class-annotated gene table written with counts reported for each of the five interaction patterns
WT-vs-KO drug log2FC scatter with identity line and interaction-significance colouring produced
Heatmap of top interaction genes across the four cells and per-gene count dot plots for the top ~12 genes produced
A quantitative detectable-effect-size statement for the interaction at n=4 per cell, 80% power, FDR<0.05, grounded in the observed dispersions, is reported
If the interaction gene set is empty at FDR<0.05, the step still produces the LFC scatter, the power statement, and the top-ranked exploratory genes, and labels them exploratory

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of interaction and within-genotype responses
caveats: GO BP sets are nested and produce blocks of correlated hits — collapse redundant terms before reporting a count
A pathway significant in the KO ranking and not in the WT ranking is not evidence of an interaction; only the interaction-ranked GSEA tests that directly
Unmapped gene symbols silently shrink the effective universe and bias enrichment
steps.context: With 12,000 genes and n=4 per cell, gene-level interaction significance may be sparse; pathway-level aggregation is where a real but modest genotype-dependent drug effect is most likely to become visible. Data is Homo sapiens brain, so human symbol-based gene sets are required.
steps.question: At the pathway level, which biological processes show a genotype-dependent drug response, and do the WT and KO drug responses engage different programmes?
constraints: Use human gene set collections only — the data is Homo sapiens; do not substitute mouse or rat collections
Rank genes by a signed statistic derived from the DESeq2 results (e.g. sign(log2FC) * -log10(pvalue) or the Wald stat); do not rank by adjusted p-value
Set minSize=15, maxSize=500, and a fixed seed
Report pathway results as hypothesis-generating; do not claim mechanism from enrichment alone
If no human gene set collection can be resolved in the environment, report the absence explicitly rather than proceeding with a substitute organism
steps.description: Run gene-set enrichment on the ranked gene lists from T1S2/T1S3 against human gene set collections: the hallmark collection and the GO biological process collection, both as human gene-symbol GMT files matching the HGNC symbols used as row names in counts.csv. Resolve these references from the environment's reference store at run time rather than assuming a path; if the GO collection is absent, proceed with hallmark alone and say so; if no human gene set collection is available at all, report that and stop the step rather than substituting a non-human collection. Run three GSEA analyses with fgsea on the shrunken-LFC-signed statistic: (a) the interaction contrast ranking (the direct pathway-level test of genotype-dependent drug response, which is more sensitive than the gene-level test), (b) drug vs vehicle within WT, (c) drug vs vehicle within KO. Report normalised enrichment scores with BH-adjusted p-values, and directly compare (b) and (c): a scatter of NES_WT vs NES_KO across pathways with the identity line, and a table of pathways whose sign or significance differs between genotypes. Cap gene set size to 15-500 members and set a fixed random seed. Output: per-analysis enrichment tables, the NES comparison table and scatter, and a bar/dot plot of the top pathways from the interaction ranking with leading-edge genes listed.
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment run against a human hallmark gene set collection at minimum, with the resolved collection named and its set count reported
GSEA results tables for the interaction ranking and for the within-WT and within-KO drug contrasts, each with NES and BH-adjusted p-values
NES_WT vs NES_KO scatter with identity line, plus a table of pathways differing in sign or significance between genotypes
Leading-edge genes reported for the top interaction-ranked pathways
Overlap between the gene symbols in counts.csv and the gene set collection reported (fraction of ranked genes mapping to any set); if below ~50% this is flagged as a symbol-nomenclature problem
Fixed random seed reported so the fgsea result is reproducible

plan.title: KO x drug interaction DE in human brain RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative: The question — does the drug act differently in KO than in WT — is exactly the genotype:treatment interaction term of a 2x2 factorial. The input is a 12,000-gene x 16-sample raw salmon count matrix (counts.csv, first column gene symbol) with a 16-row metadata table carrying genotype (WT, KO), treatment (vehicle, drug) and a combined condition label; human brain, 4 replicates per cell. The plan therefore proceeds: (T1S1) build a DESeq2 object with the full ~genotype*treatment model, verify the metadata-to-column correspondence and factor reference levels (WT, vehicle), filter low-count genes, and produce QC (library sizes, VST PCA coloured by genotype and treatment, sample-sample distances) so that any outlier or mislabelled sample is known before inference; (T1S2) the primary inference — the interaction coefficient genotypeKO:treatmentdrug with LRT-vs-Wald cross-check, plus the three interpretable simple/main contrasts (drug-vs-vehicle within WT, drug-vs-vehicle within KO, and their difference) using the cell-means parameterisation so every contrast comes from one fitted dispersion model; (T1S3) classify genes into interaction patterns (KO-specific response, WT-specific response, shared, opposite-direction/antagonistic) with explicit counting of how many genes reach FDR<0.05 on the interaction term, because with n=4 per cell the interaction test has roughly half the effective power of a main effect and a null result is a plausible, reportable outcome rather than a failure; (T2S1) pathway-level reading of the interaction-ranked and within-genotype-ranked gene lists against human hallmark and GO gene sets, which is the level at which a modest interaction signal is most likely to be detectable. T2S1 depends on T1S2/T1S3 outputs. Sizes are tiny (12k x 16), so resources are minimal throughout. No external cohort is used; GEO was not queried because the design is self-contained and no external validation was requested.
